cands.name: Josh Pendergrass

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Albertville attorney who founded Pendergrass Law Firm in 2011 (family, juvenile, church law, estate planning) and works as a pastor. His campaign site says he was Communications Director for Gov. Kay Ivey. Republican nominee for Alabama House District 69 in 2026. No elected office held.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Pendergrass was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no stated positions or actions from him on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion or education. His campaign site talks about government transparency, the Trump agenda and DOGE, and voter integrity, but does not take positions on those topics. We found no independent confirmation of his time as Communications Director for Gov. Ivey or his legal and pastoral work. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements, and he did not complete its candidate survey.

cands.name: Kelvin J Lawrence

top: Alabama Voice Of Teachers For Education
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Democrat who has represented Alabama House District 69 since November 2014. Former mayor of Hayneville (2012–2014). Homebuilder, president of Kelvin Developing Co., Inc., and owner of several Subway franchises.

controversies.text: In July 2024, Lawrence was arrested and indicted on two felony counts: second-degree forgery and possessing a forged instrument. The indictment alleges he falsified a builder's license with intent to defraud. He pleaded not guilty on July 26, 2024. The most recent report found (January 2025) still showed the case pending. No verdict was found.

endorsements.text: Recommended in the Tabitha's List: Candidates You Can Trust voter guide (a Sway voting group), per Ballotpedia.
Recommended in the Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy voter guide (a Sway voting group), per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Lawrence was born or any details of his upbringing beyond his campaign site calling him a lifelong Hayneville resident. We found no documented actions or stated positions from him on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, campaign money, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site lists only broad priorities: affordability, clean water, and healthcare and education access. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2022 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no public statements by him on data centers or development. We could not find how his 2024 forgery case ended. We found no foreign ties.
